name: Concordia University
overview:
ADDITIONAL PROGRAMME SPECIFICS

  • Programme fee of 18 590€ for non French/Belgian nationalities
  • TOEFL iBT 90 or IELTS Academic 7.0 or DET (Duolingo) score of 120 and above with no subscore under 90


_____________________________________________________________________


CONCORDIA UNIVERSITY

Concordia is a large university located in Montreal, Quebec (Canada). It has two campuses approximately seven kilometers apart:

  • Sir George Williams Campus – located in downtown Montreal
  • Loyola Campus – located in a residential area in the west of the city

They are linked by a free shuttle service available to students, teachers and staff.

The university has about 40,000 students.


Academic Vision

The university claims to have always favored access to higher education and to give priority to the person. Its mandate is to offer:

  • Excellent study programs
  • High-caliber research activities
  • Courses geared to the needs of the population


Living in Montreal

Montreal is a very beautiful city. You are also free to enjoy the pleasures of the countryside by going to the Laurentians or the Eastern Townships. You can:

  • Go sailing
  • Go skiing
  • Or simply admire the beauty of the landscape

All of this is possible within an hour or two from downtown.

administrative:
1. Application Dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline).

If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet, please be patient.


To be given to Epitech bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


Documents you will need to take with you:

  • Certified copies of the bachelor's degree and the transcript of the bachelor
  • CAQ and proof of obtaining a study permit

Please note: upon arrival, you will be asked to provide official copies of all transcripts and diplomas obtained (i.e. your baccalaureate diploma and transcript) at the Office of the Registrar.


2. Visa

The steps must be taken at the green light from the University, because the procedures can take a long time. Check out updated information directly on the university's website.

Once you have your admission letter in hand, you must obtain:

  • The Quebec Acceptance Certificate for studies (CAQ), issued by the government of Quebec (At the expense of the student: 120$ CA) The application of the CAQ must be done online and takes approximately 4 weeks to be issued. The steps to apply for the CAQ:
  • Go to: www.immigration-quebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/electronic-services/caq-electronic/index.html
  • Complete the online CAQ application
  • Print:
  • Declaration and commitment form (must be signed)
  • The personalized checklist
  • Review and ensure you have the appropriate support documents – remember to include ALL pages of your Offer of Admission.
  • We boldly recommend that you mail your application package with all supporting documents by express mail to the address indicated on the personalized checklist.


Note: Whether you apply online or mail your application, you must mail the required documents to MIFI's Montréal office, regardless of your current place of residence. Your application will not be considered until all supporting documents have been received, so don't delay. Processing time is 4 to 6 weeks!


The bank letter in French will be required for the CAQ request (see corresponding paragraph below). As an indication, the minimum amount requested in 2026 is 24 617CA $ . Please follow the sample letter available by clicking here. For the tuition fees, you will pay those of Epitech.


PLEASE NOTE: if the bank letter is not in your name but that of your parents, for example, you must attach the declaration of financial support (you must also attach it for the CAQ request): http://www.immigration-quebec.gouv.qc.ca/publications/fr/etudes/D09.pdft


  • The study permit, issued by Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada – IRCC (Cost to be borne by the student: 150 $ CA + 85$ for biometrics fee). Once you have received the electronic version of your CAQ, immediately apply for your Study Permit. The application must be done online on the IRCC website. This study permit application automatically includes a visa or Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) at no additional cost.


  • Apply online: https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/apply.html The IRCC website allows you to pay fees, apply for the study permit, and verify the status of your application.
  • Estimated process time: 12 weeks.
  • Guide: Guide 5269 – Présenter une demande de permis d’études de l‘extérieur du Canada - Canada.ca


  • Biometrics: Citizens of all countries except the United States and other minor exceptions have to give their biometrics to obtain a visa or permit.
  • You will receive an "instruction letter" in your MyCIC account with instructions to submit your biometrics at a collection service point.
  • More info: https://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/information/ou-fournir-donnees-biometriques.asp


  • Medical exam:
  • Students who reside or have resided for six months or more in the past year in certain countries need a medical exam by a IRCC-approved physician. You should allow at least one month for this process.
  • TRV or eTA:
  • Citizens of certain countries must obtain a temporary resident visa (TRV) or eTA. A TRV is placed in your passport; an eTA is linked electronically.
  • Designated learning institution number (PST):
  • On your study permit form (imm1294f), indicate the level of study as "University Baccalaureate" and include your institution's PST:
  • http://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/etudier/etudier-etablissements-liste.asp
  • AVE (eTA) check:
  • Upon receiving your document, check your Electronic Travel Authorization (AVE) number. If it does not appear, request one online: http://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/visiter/ave.asp
  • Processing time: 72 hours. Cost: $7.
  • Important: Start the CAQ application upon receiving your letter of admission. Delays may result in refusal of entry.


3. International Insurance

You can find here some information about the health and hospitalization insurance from Laval University for international students:

Enrolling in the health and hospitalization insurance plan for international students | Université Laval (ulaval.ca)


- Basic Social Protection

There is a specific agreement between France and Quebec for French nationals. It allows you to benefit from support for your health expenses (up to the equivalent of French student social security).


Before departure:

  • Request documents and the SE 401-Q-106 form from your French health insurance.
  • The form (pre-filled by the international relations office) is available on the intranet.
  • Send it to your local CPAM office for validation.
  • Upon receipt, check the validity period. An invalid duration requires a renewal.


Upon arrival in Quebec:

  • Register with the RAMQ using the validated form.
  • You will access RAMQ healthcare, maternity coverage, and work-related protection via the CSST.
  • Important: Submit your RAMQ certificate to the Bureau du Registraire to avoid being billed for the university's insurance and late fees.


- Social Protection and Complementary Health

You must also take out international insurance covering medical/hospital expenses and repatriation.


Suggested providers:

  • ACS: Sandra Zagzag – szagzag@acs-ami.com / 01.40.47.91.02
  • AVI: Afida Koucha – akoucha@avi-international.com / 01.44.63.51.32

Make sure to mention you are an EPITECH student for special rates.


Note: Non-French foreign students must take out insurance for international students from the university.


It is advisable to register on the French register established outside of France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform.

accomodation:
Students with "Visiting" status cannot access university housing at Concordia University. You may consult:

  • https://www.csu.qc.ca/resources/hojo/
  • https://www.concordia.ca/campus-life/life-in-montreal/renting-in-montreal.html


Housing basics in Quebec:

  • Room count (e.g. 4½, 5½):
  • 4½ = 2 bedrooms, 1 kitchen, 1 living room + 1 bathroom
  • 5½ = 3 bedrooms, 1 kitchen, 1 living room + 1 bathroom
  • Heating/electricity:
  • "n-ch, n-é" = not included; expect to pay $80–$120 monthly
  • Confirm with landlord if included
  • Furniture:
  • "Semi-furnished" = stove + refrigerator only
  • Furnished apartments are rare
  • Telecom:
  • Expect $100–$120/month for basic trio (landline, internet, cable)
  • Local calls are free; long-distance are charged
  • Some phones from outside Quebec may not work here

Finding accommodation:

  • http://getyourplace.com
  • https://www.kijiji.ca/h-grand-montreal/80002
  • https://rentals.ca/
courses:
Academic Requirements

You must take 24 local credits over the year, i.e., 12 credits per semester.

The courses are theoretical and given in English within the Gina Cody School of Engineering and Computer Science.


IMPORTANT: Once you have received your Concordia admission letter, you must contact the partner university to make your course choices.


EPITECH will pay the tuition fees at Concordia up to 24 credits, which are required per year to allow you to acquire the necessary credits. Any additional module you wish to take will be at your own expense.


The curriculum is intense and the level is very high. A very good level of mathematics, a good GPA, and a very good level of English are required.


You will need to provide a certificate of official English test:

  • IELTS Academic: 7.0
  • TOEFL IBT: 90
  • DET (Duolingo) score of 120 and above with no subscore under 90
  • Please note that test results must be provided on your honor.


Eligible Courses

The courses validated by EPITECH are all the courses listed below at the 300 and 400 level in the following programs:

  • Computer Science (course code: COMP)
  • Software Engineering (course code: SOEN)
  • Computer Engineering (course code: COEN)

See descriptions of the modules on:

https://campus.concordia.ca/psc/pscsprd/EMPLOYEE/HRMS/c/CU_EXT.CU_CLASS_SEARCH.GBL

Please note: The following courses are NOT open to visiting students:
  • COMP 490
  • COMP 492
  • COMP 495
  • SOEN 490


COMPUTER SCIENCE

  • COMP 426 – Multicore Programming (4 credits)
  • COMP 472 – Artificial Intelligence (4 credits)
  • COMP 473 – Pattern Recognition (4 credits) – High level of mathematics concerning probability and statistics
  • COMP 474 – Intelligent Systems (4 credits)
  • COMP 476 – Advanced Game Development (4 credits)
  • COMP 477 – Animation for Computer Games (4 credits)
  • COMP 353 – Databases (4 credits)
  • COMP 428 – Parallel Programming (4 credits)
  • COMP 478 – Image Processing (4 credits) – Attention to the level in mathematics and prerequisite in physics
  • COMP 376 – Introduction to Game Development (4 credits)
  • COMP 326 – Computer Architecture (3 credits)
  • COMP 445 – Data Communication and Computer Networks (4 credits)


SOFTWARE ENGINEERING

  • SOEN 487 – Web Services & Applications (4 credits)
  • SOEN 343 – Software Architecture and Design I (3 credits)
  • SOEN 357 – User Interface Design (3 credits)
  • SOEN 384 – Management, Measurement and Quality Control (3 credits)
  • SOEN 345 – Software Testing, Verification and Quality Assurance (3 credits)
  • SOEN 448 – Management of Evolving Systems (3 credits)
  • SOEN 321 – Information Systems Security (3 credits)

COMPUTER ENGINEERING

  • COEN 421 – Embedded Systems and Software Design (4 credits)
  • COEN 432 – Applied Genetic and Evolutionary Systems (3 credits)
Note: Course lists are given for information only. They can change from year to year. If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
For information, the courses fill up very quickly at Concordia. Once admitted, you will need to be reactive when course registration begins.
Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student’s expense (impact on credits). The classes are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.

EIP Requirement

EIP: Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP!

Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance them.

  • Food: 250 to 300 $ CAD/month
  • Transportation: 60 $ CAD/month (Opus Card)
  • Telephone: 60 $ CAD/month
  • Insurance: 40€ / month
